bivariate_pairs.rationale: Higher alcohol content is classically associated with higher perceived wine quality; check strength/direction of the relationship.
Volatile acidity (acetic acid) produces vinegar-like off-flavors; expected to degrade quality.
Sulphates act as antioxidants/antimicrobials and may positively influence quality ratings.
Citric acid adds freshness; plausible positive contribution to sensory quality.
Excess SO2 can impart pungent aromas; test whether high levels hurt quality.
Sugar directly increases solution density; key physical confounder of density.
Fermentation converts sugar to alcohol (less dense than water); density and alcohol should be inversely related and jointly confound other tests.
pH is a logarithmic measure of acid concentration; fixed (non-volatile) acids should drive pH down.
Winemakers balance freshness (citric) against spoilage acids (volatile); check for trade-off.
Free SO2 is a subset of total SO2; verify structural dependence and dispersion of the bound fraction.
